transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I've ruined things for everyone. I've been falling behind at work, and I've kind of lost control of the apartment situation. It just really feels like I deserve whatever bad thing happens next.
How long have you been feeling this way — that you've ruined things and that you deserve bad things to happen?

It's been... about a year and two months now. It really started ever since a pipe burst at my old place. That forced me to move into this much smaller apartment, and... well, all my daily routines just completely fell apart after that.
Before the pipe burst happened about a year ago, had you ever experienced a period of several weeks or more where you felt depressed, hopeless, or lost interest in things you normally enjoyed?

No, not before the pipe burst. I mean, I had normal bad days, but nothing like this. It's really just been since then. Now... most days I just wake up with this flat, heavy sadness. It's like the things that used to reset me after a long day—putting on a record, cooking, or just tinkering with some old electronics—they just don't reach me anymore. But before a year ago, no, I never had a period where I felt like that.

When the pipe burst and you had to move, did your low mood and loss of interest in things feel like a natural reaction to that stressful event, or did it feel like something that came on its own—almost like your brain chemistry changed—separate from just dealing with the move itself?

I'm not really sure. I mean, the move was definitely stressful, and it felt like a reaction to that at first. But I don't know if it was just the stress or if something else changed... it's hard to tell where the stress of the move ended and this feeling began. It just all kind of blurred together.

If the move and apartment situation were somehow resolved or improved tomorrow, do you think this heavy sadness and loss of interest would go away, or do you feel like it would stay with you regardless?

I honestly don't know. I guess I'd like to think that if I got my old place back, or if the apartment situation was just fixed, I'd feel better. But... I'm not sure anymore. It feels so heavy right now, like it's just dug in. I really couldn't tell you if fixing the apartment would actually make this go away.

Over this past year and two months, have there been any stretches of time—say, a week or two or more—where your mood lifted noticeably and you felt notably better, or has this heavy sadness been pretty much there every day without real breaks?

No, there haven't really been any breaks. It's been pretty constant. I mean, maybe a day here or there where it's slightly less heavy, but definitely not a whole week or two where I felt noticeably better. It's just been there, pretty much every day, for the whole time.
When the pipe burst happened and you had to move, did your mood drop right away—like within days or a week or two? Or did it take longer to develop, or come on gradually over weeks after the move?

I... I'm really not sure exactly when it started. It's hard to remember those first few weeks clearly. I don't know if it hit me right away or if it just sort of crept up on me while I was trying to figure everything out. It just feels like it's been this way for a long time.

Looking back, do you think your mood started getting noticeably worse within the first few weeks after the pipe burst, or did it take several months before you really felt this heavy sadness taking over?

I think it was pretty soon after. Like I said, it's hard to pin down the exact day, but looking back, this whole thing has been going on for about a year and two months. It really started right after the pipe burst, when I was forced into that smaller apartment and all my normal routines just completely fell apart.

When you think back to right after the pipe burst and move, do you think the heaviness and sadness you developed was a direct response to dealing with that specific crisis—like your mood made sense given what you were going through—or did it feel more like a separate problem that just happened to start around that same time?

I mean, it definitely felt tied to the move. It made sense to me that I was feeling so down because everything was just... upended. I lost my space, my routine was gone, and I was just trying to manage this crisis. So, yeah, I'd say it felt like a direct response to what I was going through, not just some random thing that happened at the same time.

Looking back over this past year and two months, has your mood and these feelings gotten worse even during times when the apartment situation or your routines were actually going better, or has your mood stayed pretty much tied to how things are going with your living situation?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. Um... there haven't exactly been times when the apartment situation or my routine was actually going better. It's just been kind of a constant mess since I had to move. So... I haven't really had a chance to see if I'd still feel this bad when things are going well, because things just haven't been good at all.

Besides the heavy sadness and loss of interest in things you used to enjoy, have you noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, energy levels, concentration at work, or feelings of guilt or worthlessness over this past year and two months?

Well, sleep has definitely been a big problem. I'll just lie there for hours... listening for any noises in the apartment. It takes forever to finally fall asleep, and then I always seem to wake up way before dawn. I wake up already feeling tense and exhausted, like my brain just never really powered down for the night. As for the other stuff... my energy is just gone most days, but the sleep thing is probably the most obvious change.

When you're lying there for hours before you can fall asleep, what's going through your mind? Are you mostly worried or anxious about things—like noises in the apartment or other concerns—or is it more that your mind just feels restless and you can't shut it off, even when you're not thinking about anything specific?

It's mostly worry, I guess. I'm just... I'm listening to every little creak or sound in the building. I keep thinking something else is going to break, or that maybe someone is moving around out there. My mind just kind of loops on all the things that are wrong with the place, or what could go wrong next. It's not just a blank restlessness, it's definitely tied to worrying about the apartment and feeling like I have to stay alert.

Before the pipe burst, or even right after it happened, did you ever struggle with anxiety or worry about things in general—like being alert to sounds or things going wrong—or is this hypervigilance and worry about the apartment something that really only started as part of all this?

No, I... I never really had issues with anxiety or worrying like this before. Before the pipe burst, I slept fine. I didn't care about normal apartment noises. This whole thing with being on edge and listening for every little sound... that really just started after the apartment flooded and everything kind of fell apart. I was never like this before.

If you think about the sadness, the loss of interest in things, the sleep problems, and this worry about the apartment—do all of these feel like they're fundamentally about struggling to cope with what happened with the move and the apartment situation, or do some of these symptoms feel like they've taken on a life of their own, separate from just reacting to that stressor?

I'm not really sure how to answer that. I guess... I haven't really thought about it that way. It's hard to tell where the stress about the apartment ends and everything else begins. 

I mean, it all started with the pipe bursting and everything getting ruined, so to me it just feels like it's all tied to that. I don't really know if the sadness or the sleep issues have taken on a life of their own or not... I just know I can't seem to snap out of it. It all just feels like one big heavy cloud that hasn't lifted since it happened.

If someone else had experienced the exact same thing—their apartment flooded, they lost their home, their routines fell apart—would you think it would be normal for them to feel this depressed and anxious for a year, or does it seem like your reaction has been more severe or longer-lasting than what most people would go through?

I don't really know. I guess... I mean, losing your home is a big deal, so I think anyone would be pretty upset and stressed out about it. But a whole year? I don't know if most people would still be this stuck. Maybe they'd have figured out a way to move on or get back to normal by now. For me, it just feels like I can't get past it, but I really couldn't say what's normal for someone else.

Over this past year, have there been any times when your apartment situation actually improved or felt more manageable—even temporarily—and if so, did your mood and anxiety improve along with it, or did they stay pretty much the same regardless?

Well, there haven't really been any improvements with the apartment situation. It's just been an ongoing mess with the insurance and the contractors, so nothing has really felt more manageable. It's just been a constant source of stress. So, I haven't really had a chance to see if my mood would get better if the apartment stuff got sorted out. It's just been bad the whole time.

Let me ask you this directly: if by some miracle your old apartment was fully restored tomorrow, or you found an amazing new place that felt like home and got your routines back exactly as they were before—do you think this heavy sadness and the way you feel about yourself would go away, or do you sense that this depression might stay with you even if the apartment problem was completely solved?

I honestly don't know. I mean... I'd like to think that if everything was suddenly fixed and I had my home back, I'd feel like myself again. But it's been so long now. I'm not sure if just fixing the apartment would be like flipping a switch to turn off all this sadness. It feels pretty heavy at this point, so... yeah, I really couldn't say for sure if it would all just go away or if it would stay with me.

When you think about how you felt in those first few weeks right after the pipe burst—before things had time to settle or get worse—did you already feel this same heavy sadness and hopelessness, or did it gradually get worse and worse as the months went on?

Well, it didn't all hit me at once. Right after the pipe burst... I was mostly just scrambling, you know? Just trying to figure out where to sleep and what to do with my stuff. But as time went on, and I got stuck in this smaller place and all my routines just completely fell apart... that's when it really started getting heavy. It's been about a year and two months now since it happened, and it just feels like it's been slowly dragging me further down the whole time.

You mentioned that right after the pipe burst you were mostly just scrambling, and then over the months it got heavier and heavier. But I want to ask you this: over these past year and two months, even on days when you weren't actively dealing with apartment problems or thinking about the move, did you still feel that heavy sadness and hopelessness, or was it mainly when you were dealing with apartment-related stress?

It's pretty much there all the time, even when I'm not dealing with the apartment stuff. Most days I wake up with this... just this flat, heavy sadness. It's like the things that used to reset me or make me feel better—like putting on a record, cooking a meal, or tinkering with my electronics—they just don't reach me anymore. It doesn't matter if I'm actively stressed about the move or not, that heaviness is just kind of sitting there.
